subject: Catalyst private deployment: linkage paths (VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN) — decision request

Subject: Catalyst private deployment: linkage paths (VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN) — decision request

Tom — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our call, I put together a short summary of the three connectivity patterns we discussed and a pragmatic recommendation for Catalyst's initial rollout. I attached a comparison matrix (catalyst_linkage_matrix.xlsx) and a draft MOU for reference.

High-level options we covered:
- VPC Peering: low-latency, simple routing if Catalyst will peer directly to our infra account; no cross-account PrivateLink needed. Limited to same-region or specific cloud accounts; blast radius can be larger because routing is direct.
- AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints): strong isolation (no route table exposure), easier cross-account access and least blast radius; steady-state latency usually slightly higher than peering but predictable; better for regulated workloads.
- Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN: fast to set up for on-prem, encrypted over internet; variable latency; good for admin/metrics & tooling traffic but less ideal for low-latency, high-TPS inference traffic at scale.

Questions for you to confirm before we lock the pattern:
1) Do you prefer an encrypted internet-based tunnel (S2S) initially while the peering/private link is provisioned?
2) Expected steady-state QPS to Redwood API (p95 tokens/sec or requests/sec) and whether traffic is mostly small inference calls (~512 tokens) or larger batch inference.
3) Compliance constraints: you mentioned HITRUST-ish controls — does Catalyst require zero internet egress for inference traffic?

Initial recommendation (tentative): PrivateLink for production inference endpoints + S2S VPN for admin/metrics and emergency access. PrivateLink gives the cleanest security boundary and makes audits simpler; S2S accelerates onboarding. VPC Peering is only attractive if Catalyst wants full-layer routing between VPCs (and accepts larger blast radius).

Next steps I propose if you agree:
- Confirm QPS and compliance constraint (answers to #2 and #3)
- We'll deliver an architecture diagram and a proposed cutover window (I uploaded a sketch: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgCatalyst-arch-diagram)
- Legal: sign the attached MOU to allow infra porting and account-level peering work (draft_mou.pdf)

Thanks — I’ll wait for your go/no-go on PrivateLink as primary and whether you want VPN as an interim.

— Priya

Priya / Tom — adding a few technical points so the decision is fully informed. (Inline notes and a short recommendation at the end.)

VPC Peering
- Pros: minimal per-request overhead, native routing between accounts.
- Cons: cross-account peering requires route table changes, risk of accidental exposure (ACCEPT/REJECT rules), not transitive. If Catalyst runs multiple on-prem edges in different regions, you need multiple peerings.
- Ops: IP management is important — avoid overlapping CIDRs.

PrivateLink
- Pros: per-service interface endpoints with explicit security groups; works across accounts/roles; best isolation for compliance. Fits well if Redwood exposes inference as an NLB+interface endpoint.
- Cons: adds an extra hop (ENI -> NLB -> service), slight latency delta (~2–10ms typical); per-GB hourly endpoint charges on AWS are a consideration for high-throughput customers.
- Ops: we need to publish endpoint service name; Catalyst must create interface endpoints in their VPC. Works well with dedicated subnets for ENIs and with our TLS mTLS options.

Site-to-Site VPN
- Pros: fast to bring up, works for on-prem, can carry management traffic.
- Cons: jitter and variable latency; scaling throughput requires multiple tunnels or AWS Direct Connect which has longer lead times; not ideal as only path for high-QPS inference.

Recommendation
- For Catalyst's stated needs (strict audit boundary, moderate-to-high inference QPS, on-prem offices in SF and Austin): Primary: PrivateLink for production inference. Secondary: S2S VPN as a warm standby for admin channels + quick onboarding. VPC Peering only if Catalyst wants fully routed private mesh (and can commit to CIDR planning).

Operational notes
- Egress billing: track per-GB; PrivateLink reduces cross-account NAT egress in some designs but interface endpoints have per-hour costs.
- Fallover: we can configure client-side fallback to a hosted public endpoint if PrivateLink/NLB health fails; we'll coordinate failover TTLs and DNS TTLs with Catalyst.

I attached a short checklist for infra (IP ranges, subnets, required service quotas) in the shared drive — Priya, please push that to the customer.

— Karthik

Thanks Priya, Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Compliance: we need evidence that inference traffic never traverses public internet in plaintext and that the control plane is auditable. HITRUST is the long-term goal though right now it’s SOC2 + some HSP-type controls. PrivateLink sounds much better for that.
2) Latency: our production SLA needs p95 request latency under 120ms to end-to-end from our app tier (SF) to inference. Most calls are small (~200–400 tokens), but we expect spikes during batch runs.
3) On-prem footprint: we have an office in Austin with a fixed public IP for the firewall; an S2S tunnel there is trivial to set up and will help with metrics.

Decision: we’re aligned with your recommendation — go with PrivateLink as the primary path for inference traffic. Please provision a PrivateLink onboarding checklist and share the architecture diagram. We also want S2S VPN into a management VPC for metrics, agent updates, and emergency RDP.

Next asks:
- Can you provide a short runbook for the PrivateLink creation steps and expected bandwidth/cost estimate?
- Any recommended DNS patterns and client SDK fallback behavior for PrivateLink health failures?

If you can get a proposed cutover weekend and runbook by Friday, we can get infra approval on our end.

— Tom

Director of Engineering, Catalyst Systems
